entries.excerpt: Accurate copying of nucleic acid sequences is essential for self-replicating systems. Modern cells achieve error ratios as low as 10−9 with sophisticated enzymes capable of kinetic proofreading. In contrast, experiments probing enzyme-free copying of RNA and DNA as potential prebiotic replication processes find error ratios on the order of 10%. entries.title: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory
entries.excerpt: Emerging evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to visual short-term memory (VSTM). However, the neural mechanisms through which hippocampal activity supports the maintenance of VSTM representations remain largely unknown. Here, using intracranial EEG recordings from human participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task for naturalistic objects, we investigated the role of hippocampal ripple activity—brief high-frequency oscillations associated with memory replay—in VSTM maintenance and hippocampal-neocortical communication. We found that hippocampal ripple rates progressively ramped up during the maintenance period and supported successful VSTM. More critically, hippocampal ripples were temporally coupled with the ripples in the lateral temporal lobe (LTL), and these coupled ripples were associated with memory reactivation in the LTL. These findings provide direct evidence that hippocampal–neocortical interaction via coupled ripples supports VSTM, extending the role of hippocampal ripples from long-term consolidation to short-term mnemonic processes and offering new insights into the dynamic coding mechanisms of working memory.

entries.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
entries.excerpt: Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity. In the absence of GDI-1 SUMOylation, GDI-1 binds to GDP-RAB-1, sequestering it in the cytoplasm, resulting in impaired phagosomal degradation. Furthermore, we found SUMOylation of GDI1 at a conserved site plays a crucial role in efferocytosis regulation in mammals. This study defines a previously unrecognized mechanism by which SUMOylation drives apoptotic cell clearance.

entries.title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
entries.excerpt: How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. groups.summary: Accurate copying of nucleic acid sequences is essential for self-replicating systems. Modern cells achieve error ratios as low as 10−9 with sophisticated enzymes capable of kinetic proofreading. In contrast, experiments probing enzyme-free copying of RNA and DNA as potential prebiotic replication processes find error ratios on the order of 10%. Given this low intrinsic copying fidelity, plausible scenarios for the spontaneous emergence of molecular evolution require an accuracy-enhancing mechanism. groups.title: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory
groups.summary: Emerging evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to visual short-term memory (VSTM). However, the neural mechanisms through which hippocampal activity supports the maintenance of VSTM representations remain largely unknown. Here, using intracranial EEG recordings from human participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task for naturalistic objects, we investigated the role of hippocampal ripple activity—brief high-frequency oscillations associated with memory replay—in VSTM maintenance and hippocampal-neocortical communication. We found that hippocampal ripple rates progressively ramped up during the maintenance period and supported successful VSTM. More critically, hippocampal ripples were temporally coupled with the ripples in the lateral temporal lobe (LTL), and these coupled ripples were associated with memory reactivation in the LTL. These findings provide direct evidence that hippocampal–neocortical interaction via coupled ripples supports VSTM, extending the role of hippocampal ripples from long-term consolidation to short-term mnemonic processes and offering new insights into the dynamic coding mechanisms of working memory.

groups.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
groups.summary: Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity. In the absence of GDI-1 SUMOylation, GDI-1 binds to GDP-RAB-1, sequestering it in the cytoplasm, resulting in impaired phagosomal degradation. Furthermore, we found SUMOylation of GDI1 at a conserved site plays a crucial role in efferocytosis regulation in mammals. This study defines a previously unrecognized mechanism by which SUMOylation drives apoptotic cell clearance.

sources.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
sources.excerpt: Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity. In the absence of GDI-1 SUMOylation, GDI-1 binds to GDP-RAB-1, sequestering it in the cytoplasm, resulting in impaired phagosomal degradation. Furthermore, we found SUMOylation of GDI1 at a conserved site plays a crucial role in efferocytosis regulation in mammals. This study defines a previously unrecognized mechanism by which SUMOylation drives apoptotic cell clearance.

groups.title: Altitude-induced hypoxia suppresses Varroa mite reproduction in Tibetan honey bees
groups.summary: Our reliance on honey bees ( Apis mellifera ) for pollination services and honey production continues to increase due to the global decline in other pollinators and rising demand for honey. The ectoparasitic mite ( Varroa destructor ) remains the biggest pest of honey bees forcing beekeepers into continual miticide use. Beekeepers on the Tibetan Plateau, however, report rarely seeing mites in their colonies, unlike all other areas of China. We conducted a series of translocation experiments to investigate this phenomenon. groups.title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
groups.summary: How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. Using a simple hierarchical tumor model in Drosophila , we show that differentiation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) into transit amplifying progenitors (TAPs) depends on the fraction of TAPs among their immediate neighbors. This relationship is captured by a local feedback transition rule that quantitatively predicts CSC transition probability. Implementing this rule in 3D growth simulations spontaneously recapitulates CSC clustering and the emergence of a stable CSC fraction within tumors. Mechanistically, the local feedback is mediated by EGFR signaling from newly produced TAPs, propagating differentiation across CSC clusters. Consistently, we show that clustering protects the CSC pool from depletion driven by surrounding TAPs, indicating that spatial architecture and lineage dynamics are tightly coupled. groups.title: Migration as a key influence on ungulate eco-evolutionary history
groups.summary: Species can overcome resource limitations by migrating to more favourable areas. A new study in PLOS Biology shows that migration has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, that likely led to changes in ecosystem functioning. Species can overcome environmental limitations by migrating to more favorable areas. This Primer explores a new study in PLOS Biology showing that this behavior has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, which in turn likely led to changes in ecosystem properties and functioning.
groups.fullTextSummary: However, the consequences of migration over longer timescales are less clear: while species that can accurately track the changes in environmental/biological resources might benefit from migration by potentially decreasing extinction rates, failing to accurately track resources can lead to an increase in the extinction probability, due to food shortage, increased predation while migrating, and mismatches with environment conditions. Another key result from the paper was that the increased extinction rates were associated with a decrease in the total volume of the ecomorphospace (a form of representation in which each point represents the combination of different characteristics of a given species) occupied by ungulates, due particularly to the loss of migratory species, which were more prevalent amongst recently extinct species than amongst contemporary species.
